status: Review draft; fictional scenarios with historical benchmarks, not current procurement estimates

ons.limitation: General CPI adjustment is a teaching approximation, not a construction-cost index.

glass.scope: Glass cleaning/refining for insulation. Capital scale comparator only; the draft assumes a separate container-remelt outlet.

plastics.scope: Pre-sorted rigid plastics washed and flaked; historical plant closed in 2024. Annual capacity of 20000 in draft is 70 x 285 operating days, rounded, not a reported annual nameplate figure.

food.scope: Bygrave Lodge food-waste AD. Project benchmark, not a quotation for the fictional catchment.

defra.unit: kg CO2e per metric tonne managed
defra.scope: Historical consumption-based waste-treatment model; processing/transport and displacement credits included. Do not add separate energy credits. Capital construction emissions not modelled.

decc.scope: Costs are independent benchmark selections, not measured paired designs. Automation can reduce operating labour. Feedstock costs and gate-fee revenues excluded.

garden.scope: Crewe in-vessel composting with outdoor composting and screening; real plant accepts mixed food/garden waste. Scenario uses separately collected garden waste only, avoiding overlap with Food.

table_9.scope: Transport from collection points to treatment, containers, treatment and hazardous-waste/residue handling; primary material revenue included. Initial household/retailer collection excluded. This is a purchased service benchmark, not gross plant operating expense.

table_77.accounting: Consumption-based Carbon WARM model used by Anthesis; not the territorial Table 16 used in the main IA monetary appraisal.

weee.scope: Historical indicative model; no claim about current legal requirements. Scenario assumes suitable, non-reusable small electricals with a comparable material mix and closed-loop outlets.

starter.capital_rounding: Glass, Plastics and Food: nearest GBP 4m after CPI conversion; Garden: nearest GBP 1m. Each rounded value differs from the converted benchmark by under 6%.

electrical.treatment: specialist material recycling, comparable to the Table 77 closed-loop mix
electrical.service_derivation: 75 * 133.9 / 107.8 * 5000 / 1000000 = 0.465793 million; rounded to 0.5 million per year
electrical.scope: Separate checked scenario flow after reuse assessment; an existing processor supplies reserved capacity. No new electrical plant capital cost. Net service payment is added once; material income is not separately credited.

clues: A does not have the lowest building cost
A costs less to build than B
The lowest-build-cost plan has the highest annual cost
Exactly one: B building cost is 20; B annual cost is 0.5
cost_grid.scoring: Three points for both complete correct grids; replaces the three separate cost-entry questions. Budget shortlist still requires five-year calculations.

assumptions: Both activities use the same fictional city and surrounding-town catchment, approximately 500000 residents plus businesses. This is an authored scale assumption, not measured local data.
Material availability, the survey, delivery records, budgets and targets are authored scenario inputs; they are not findings reported by the benchmark sources.
The longer scenario is an alternative decision exercise, not a sequel to a plant already built in the starter.

Plants receive pre-separated suitable material; stated tonnages are managed input to the chosen treatment route. Historical emissions factors already include average process burdens/yields; no second yield adjustment.
Glass/plastics have outlets replacing equivalent virgin raw materials. Savings are relative to the specified route, not a universal material ranking.

Food running costs are fixed gross allowances with no food revenue assumed. Electrical treatment is a separately purchased net service including primary material revenue; no electrical capital or second revenue credit is added. Financing, price changes, land and initial collection are excluded. The comparison is the partnership’s budget outlay, not operators’ gross production costs.

Design flow/electrical-capacity pairings are authored scale checks, not rated manufacturer specifications. A 0.9/1.5/2 MW class for 20/30/45 ktpa is plausible against the Bygrave-scale benchmark but not independently engineered.
Linear benefit per tonne is a classroom model, not evidence of identical fixed plant burdens at different utilisation.
Environmental target concerns estimated treatment savings, not full construction lifecycle or a complete statutory waste-management plan.
